issues.on_page: Trimmed PDF skips report p9 (trimmed p4 = report p8, p5 = report p10), report p12 (trimmed p6 = report p11, p7 = report p13) and report p40 (trimmed p15 = report p39, p16 = report p41)
issues.issue: Trim gap, not an extraction error. pp9/12 are probably the fund-to-government-wide reconciliations. p40 sits between the General Fund and Logan East budget schedules and may be a Sinking Fund or other budget schedule (the notes say the Sinking Fund isn't in the trimmed PDF). Every trimmed page (1-17 of 17) is fully covered and every printed total ties.

The GAAP line probably also holds state-paid homestead (66,988), property tax credit (515,448), pro-rate motor vehicle (10,482) and nameplate capacity tax (46,840), which the budgetary schedule p13 shows separately. It can't be split because no page breaks down this line. Kept as property tax with a review note, which is defensible, but about 0.6M of state aid sits in property tax.
Chemigation fees in Nebraska NRDs are permit fees, so licenses and permits may fit better. The same applies to detail[7].
ending_cash leaves out County treasurer's accounts 35,540, which the budgetary schedule p15 counts as cash. Investments are recorded separately in ending_investments.

The extractor added a qualifier to the printed label. Also detail[52] 'Transfers (in expenditures)' is printed as 'TRANSFERS' (p15). Both sides of the 1,750,000 sit inside the same budgetary General Fund schedule (Sinking Fund activity), so the transfer nets out. Classifying it as other financing is correct.

issues.extracted: Wau-Col RWS reimbursement 975 (revenue, reimbursements/refunds); detail[88] Repayment to the Natural Resources District 975 (expenditure, grants/payments to other entities)
issues.issue: This is an interfund repayment between the General Fund and the Wau-Col enterprise fund, recorded as ordinary revenue on one side and spending on the other. It may be repayment of an interfund advance (due to/from other funds appear on pp4, 8), not true revenue or spending.

Water system hookup fees fit 'other utility charges' better (Lower Niobrara uses that category for the same line). The GAAP statement p10 treats this 32,000 as capital contributions (business_type.other_financing).
